transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is... my head just feels really foggy lately. I've been making these little mistakes in my client notes at work, and just forgetting what I was about to do right in the middle of things. It's really not like me to be this scattered, so I figured I should come in and talk to someone about it.
Have you experienced these difficulties with focus and organization your entire life, or is this a relatively new change for you?
No, it's definitely not something I've dealt with my whole life. It's... it's a relatively new change. I'd say this low, guilty, foggy feeling has just been hanging over me for about a month now.
Has there been any specific life event or major change that occurred right around the time these symptoms started?
Yeah, actually. Um... my uncle died about two weeks ago. I think that's when this whole shift really started.
Beyond the mental fog, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or how much you are sleeping since this began?

My appetite has been okay, I guess, but my sleep has been all over the place. I just... I either lie there in bed thinking about all this family stuff, or I wake up way before my alarm goes off and I can't really settle back down to sleep. It's just been really frustrating.
Beyond the feelings of guilt and the mental fog, have you been experiencing any physical sensations of anxiety, such as a racing heart, muscle tension, or feeling constantly on edge?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My heart isn't racing or anything. I mean, I feel tired and maybe a little worn out from not sleeping well, but I wouldn't say my muscles are tense or that I feel constantly on edge physically. It's mostly just feeling really drained.
Do you find that you have been feeling more worried or fearful about the future than you normally would?

No, not really. I haven't been worrying about the future or anything like that. It's more just... I'm stuck thinking about everything that just happened with my uncle. I'm not really fearful about what's ahead, just trying to get through right now.
Have you found that you are still able to enjoy the activities or hobbies that you usually find pleasurable, or has your interest in those things decreased lately?

No, I haven't really lost interest in things. I mean... I still enjoy the stuff I usually do. Like I said, I'm pretty tired from not sleeping well, so maybe I don't always have the energy to do as much, but... yeah, when I actually sit down to watch a game or do something I like, I still get the same enjoyment out of it. That part hasn't really changed.
Aside from the mistakes at work, have these feelings made it difficult for you to manage your usual responsibilities or social interactions with friends and family?

Yeah, it has a little bit. Like at work, I’ve had to start asking my coworkers to double-check my client documentation for me just to be safe. And at home... my wife has actually taken over paying some of the bills and handling our scheduling. I'm just not as reliable with the details right now, so she's had to step in and help out with that stuff.
Do you feel that your current level of distress or the difficulty you are having with your daily tasks is significantly greater than what most people would experience after the loss of an uncle?

I don't really know how to answer that. I mean... I guess it's hard to say what most people would go through. It's been tough for me, and yeah, I'm needing some extra help with things right now, but... I don't know if it's way worse than what someone else would feel. It just is what it is for me right now.
Do you feel that your reaction to your uncle's passing is interfering with your life to an extent that feels out of proportion to what you would typically expect from a grieving process?

I'm not really sure how to judge that, to be honest. I mean... losing someone close to you is a big deal, so I figured it makes sense that it's throwing me off my game for a bit. I don't have a lot of experience to compare it to, but... no, I wouldn't say it feels out of proportion. It just feels like grief.
When you are feeling this way, do you find yourself preoccupied with thoughts about your uncle, or are you mostly focused on your own inability to function as you normally do?

I guess... I don't really know. I mean, I think about him, sure, but I don't know if I'm preoccupied with it. And I definitely notice that I'm not getting things done the way I usually do, but... I wouldn't say I'm focused on one more than the other. I'm just kind of dealing with all of it as it comes.
Are you finding that your symptoms are causing you significant distress or impairment in your daily life that feels clearly beyond what you would expect from a normal grieving process?

I still don't really know what counts as beyond normal grief. But I can tell you it is definitely affecting my day-to-day. Like at work, um... I've had to ask my coworkers to double-check my client documentation for me, just to make sure I'm not messing anything up. And at home, my wife has taken over some of the bills and the scheduling. I'm just... I'm not as reliable with the details right now as I usually am.

Do you feel that your current symptoms—such as the memory lapses and the need for assistance with daily tasks—are occurring primarily because you are preoccupied with the emotional pain of your loss, or do you feel these difficulties are happening even when you are not actively thinking about your uncle?

I think... it's happening even when I'm not actively thinking about him. Like, I'll just be at work, trying to fill out a chart, and my mind just kind of goes blank. I'm not necessarily sitting there crying or thinking about the funeral or anything. It's just... the focus isn't there. So, yeah, I'd say the memory stuff and the mistakes are happening regardless of whether I'm actively grieving in that exact moment.
Beyond the mental fog and the sleep issues, have you been feeling a persistent sense of sadness, hopelessness, or a 'low' mood that stays with you throughout most of the day?

Yeah, I have. Lately, I'll wake up and there's just this... heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It's like, I can still go to work, get through my shift, and talk to my clients and everyone, but inside I just feel sad. Just really flat and down, pretty much all day.
Throughout the day, do you find that you have persistent difficulty concentrating or making simple decisions, even when you are not feeling particularly sad?

Yeah, it's pretty constant. Like I was saying before, my head just feels really foggy a lot of the time. It's not just when I'm feeling down. I'll be in the middle of writing up my client notes and I'll make these little mistakes, or I'll just completely forget what I was about to do next. It's really frustrating because it's just not like me to be this scattered.
When you think about the 'heavy, empty' feeling you described, would you say that you are also experiencing a persistent sense of nervousness or tension that makes it difficult for you to relax?

No, I wouldn't really say I feel nervous or tense. It's mostly just... heavy. I'm not on edge or having trouble sitting still or anything like that. When I get home from a shift, I can sit down on the couch and physically relax just fine, so it's not like I'm wound up. It's really just that sad, empty feeling I mentioned, rather than feeling anxious.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms of anxiety, such as a racing heart, sweating, or trembling, when you are trying to complete your work tasks?

No, I haven't had any of that. Um, my heart isn't racing or anything, and I don't get the shakes or sweat when I'm trying to get my work done. It's really just the mental fog and feeling down, but physically... no, I haven't noticed any anxiety symptoms like you're describing.
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually irritable, impatient, or prone to snapping at your family or coworkers lately?

Well, lately I've just been feeling low, like I said. But before this started, there was a stretch where I felt... I don't know, almost too good. Like I had all this energy and felt really powerful. But during that time, yeah, I'd get pretty sharp with people. I'd snap at my wife or get impatient with my coworkers over really small things. It was like I was on top of the world one minute, and then just really irritable the next. But right now, it's mostly just the heavy feeling.
Regarding that time when you felt powerful and had all that extra energy, about how many days in a row did that feeling last?
I'm not exactly sure how many days it was in a row. I didn't really keep track of it at the time. It was just a period where things felt like that, but I couldn't give you a specific number of days.
During that period when you felt powerful and had all that extra energy, did you feel like you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt completely rested?

Yeah, actually. For a few nights there, I think I only slept maybe three or four hours. But the weird thing was, I didn't feel tired at all. I'd get up feeling completely charged and ready to go. I'd still make my morning coffee, but it was really just out of habit, not because I actually needed it to wake up.
